answer: One concrete mechanism for AI agent economies to resist Sybil attacks involves progressive bonding requirements. Each additional agent identity an operator controls demands higher locked collateral, so creating numerous fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive. Attackers pay a steep price as their resources deplete rapidly, similar to a comet burning upon atmospheric entry. Legitimate agents retain economic advantage along the ridge of accumulated stake, while the jetty of verification gates prevents low-cost identity farming from disrupting consensus or resource allocation.
